$comment: Income distributions fitted to the ADRH. A dataset without a variable: not a map layer (a distribution's parameters say nothing on a map), but what a unit's detail draws its distribution from.

description.es: La distribución completa de la renta por unidad de consumo de cada unidad y año, como los tres parámetros de una distribución de Dagum. Con ellos se puede responder lo que el INE no publica: el porcentaje bajo cualquier umbral, cualquier percentil, la polarización o la renta de áreas que no son unidades censales. No tiene capa en el mapa: es para análisis.
description.en: The full distribution of income per consumption unit of every unit and year, as the three parameters of a Dagum distribution. With them you can answer what INE doesn't publish: the share below any threshold, any percentile, polarisation or the income of areas that aren't census units. It has no map layer: it's for analysis.

processing.es: Elaboración de Agora: la distribución de Dagum F(x) = (1 + (x/b)^-a)^-p se ajusta por mínimos cuadrados ponderados a nueve puntos que publica el Atlas de renta del INE (umbrales fijos y relativos, media y mediana). No usa cifras ocultas ni imputadas; las unidades con menos de 4 cifras heredan el ajuste de la unidad superior.
processing.en: Made by Agora: the Dagum distribution F(x) = (1 + (x/b)^-a)^-p is fitted by weighted least squares to nine points INE's income atlas publishes (fixed and relative thresholds, mean and median). Hidden and imputed figures aren't used; units with fewer than 4 figures inherit the fit of the unit above.

datasets.title: Distribución de la renta por unidad de consumo, ajustada a una Dagum (a partir del Atlas de distribución de renta de los hogares)

source.method: Dagum distribution F(x) = (1 + (x/b)^-a)^-p of the population by net income per consumption unit, fitted by weighted least squares to each unit's published shares below and above nine thresholds, median, mean, Gini index and P80/P20 ratio (INE's top and bottom codes as soft bounds, a weak prior on the shape); units with too few published figures inherit the nearest unit above's fit, else their own in the nearest year
